topic.title: Rule 3.6.b: does the code-sharing requirement apply to this paper track?
topic.forumName: Google - The Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track
topic.content:
Hello,

I'm preparing a research paper for the Gemma 4 Developer Agent Paper Track. The work evaluates code-graph-guided repository retrieval and a local Gemma 4 reranker, using the external Loc-Bench V1 dataset. It does not use competition-provided data.

Could you clarify whether Rule 3.6.b's requirement to share relevant competition code on Kaggle applies to this paper track when the work uses no Competition Data? In particular, would a public GitHub repository containing the benchmark implementation and documentation be permitted, or must the code also be shared through a Kaggle notebook or competition forum?

I would also appreciate clarification on whether reporting aggregate experimental metrics derived from an external dataset with no stated licence raises any specific competition eligibility concern.

Thank you.

comments.content:
Github should work for sharing code.

You should not be breaking any permissions to compete in this competition. If you have the rights to evaluate on the external dataset that should be fine.
